classification.difficultyReason: Connect the derivative, quadratic sketch and stationary point, then calculate and sketch a normal using its negative reciprocal gradient.

answer.short: An upward-opening parabola with intercepts $(0,0)$ and $(4,0)$ and minimum $(2,-4)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=x(x-4)\\f(x)&=(x-2)^2-4\end{aligned}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(0,0)$ and $(4,0)$, with minimum $(2,-4)$ and axis of symmetry $x=2$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: When is the gradient of the tangent $0$? What special significance does this point have on your graph?

answer.short: At $x=2$. The point $(2,-4)$ is the turning point (minimum) of the parabola.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=0\\2x-4&=0\\x&=2\\f(2)&=2^2-4(2)\\f(2)&=-4\end{aligned}$$
The point $(2,-4)$ is the turning point (minimum) of the parabola.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the equation of the normal to the tangent at $x=3$, and sketch it on your graph.

answer.short: $x+2y+3=0$. Sketch the line through $(3,-3)$ with gradient $-\tfrac12$ on the graph in part b.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}f'(3)&=2(3)-4\\f'(3)&=2\\f(3)&=3^2-4(3)\\f(3)&=-3\\m_{\perp}&=-\frac12\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}y-(-3)&=-\frac12(x-3)\\2y+6&=-x+3\\x+2y+3&=0\end{aligned}$$
Sketch the normal through $(3,-3)$ with gradient $-\tfrac12$ on the graph in part b.

spec.description: Shared answer graph for parts b and d: double-arrowed black axes without ticks or numerical labels, blue upward-opening parabola and descending blue normal. Plot extents are chosen for legibility rather than treated as source numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: Parabola y=x^2-4x, with zeros 0 and 4 and minimum (2,-4); normal y=-x/2-3/2 at (3,-3).
spec.answerVisibility: Answer editions only; the parabola answers part b and the normal answers part d.
